title: Jedlik Motors founder Raguram SK on building electric pod for urban commuters
summary:
Chennai-based EV startup Jedlik Motors is developing a fully enclosed electric two wheeler, e-POD, aimed at combining the maneuverability of a scooter with the comfort and safety of a car.
In an interaction with Entrackr, Raguram SK, founder and CEO of Jedlik Motors, discussed the company’s product roadmap, business model, technology, funding plans and expansion strategy.
Raguram, a mechanical engineer by background, started his entrepreneurial journey with an online electric vehicle dealership in 2019. After the business was impacted by Covid 19, he worked as a mechanical designer at an MNC before starting Jedlik Motors.
The startup is currently at the MVP stage and has developed a prototype of the e-POD. According to Raguram, the company has secured two patents, of which one has been granted and another has been published.
The e-POD is designed for urban commuters who want protection from weather conditions without compromising on the maneuverability associated with two wheelers. The vehicle is expected to feature air conditioning, pushback seats, an infotainment system and around 600 litres of boot space.
The e-POD will also feature crab walking steering, which is designed to allow tighter turns and easier maneuverability in dense urban traffic.
“Essentially, we are developing a vehicle that combines the comfort and safety of a car with the maneuverability of a motorcycle,” Raguram said.
For consumers, Jedlik Motors is targeting an on road price of around Rs 2.5 lakh. The company is also exploring a battery as a service (BaaS) model, which could bring the upfront vehicle cost down to around Rs 1.5 lakh. The battery subscription is expected to cost approximately Rs 2,000 to Rs 2,500 per month, although the final pricing is still being worked out.
Jedlik Motors is also developing a separate B2B version of the vehicle for applications such as food delivery, quick commerce and large industrial campuses. The startup has initiated conversations with companies including Mahindra, Tata Motors, Ashok Leyland and Maruti Suzuki. It is also reaching out to Rapido, Yes Madam, Tiffit and Ajego.
On the technology front, the company is developing autonomous driving capabilities along with its own motors, controllers and steer by wire systems. The autonomous driving stack is being designed to eventually operate in increasingly complex traffic conditions.
The startup currently has a team of around 10 people and carries out assembly at its Chennai facility. Around 90% to 95% of its component designs are developed in house, while battery cells are currently sourced from Taiwan or China.
Jedlik Motors plans to launch the e-POD by June 2027, starting with a pilot in Bengaluru before expanding to Chennai and other tier 1 cities. It also plans to target markets such as the UAE and other Asian countries, with broader global expansion targeted by 2030.
The company has so far received around Rs 26 lakh in government grants and Rs 47 lakh in angel funding. It is currently looking to raise Rs 7 crore in a pre-seed round to support its next phase of development.

title: AceVector’s IPO subscribed over 5X on final day
summary:
AceVector, the parent company of Snapdeal, Unicommerce and Stellaro Brands, saw decent demand for its IPO, with the issue subscribed 5.07 times as investors bid for 36.61 crore shares against 7.22 crore shares on offer.
AceVector’s initial public offering (IPO) was open for subscription from September 25-September 29, with a price band of Rs 30-32 and a minimum investment of Rs 14,040 for a lot size of 468 shares.
According to exchange data, the non-institutional investors (NIIs) portion saw the highest demand with 8.53X subscription, followed by the retail quota at 4.83X, while the Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) portion was subscribed 3.42X.
The IPO comprises a fresh issue of Rs 287 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 4.16 crore shares worth around Rs 133 crore at the upper price band.
SoftBank, Nexus Venture Partners and other existing investors will partially offload their stakes through the OFS, while co-founders Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal will not sell any shares in the IPO.
The fresh proceeds from the IPO will primarily be used for Snapdeal’s marketing and business promotion, technology infrastructure, acquisitions and general corporate purposes.

title: ITC completes 100% acquisition of Yoga Bar parent Sproutlife

FMCG major ITC has completed the acquisition of Sproutlife Foods, the parent company of nutrition and healthy foods brand Yoga Bar, after acquiring the remaining stake in the Bengaluru based company.

title: Bewakoof’s revenue jumps 40% to Rs 243 Cr in FY26, losses rise 19%
summary:
Following a modest 7% growth in FY25, Aditya Birla Group-owned Bewakoof posted a strong 40% year-on-year growth in operating revenue in FY26. At the same time, the D2C fashion brand’s losses increased 19% during the fiscal year ended March 2026.
Bewakoof’s operating revenue rose 40.5% to Rs 243 crore in FY26 from Rs 173 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).


Bewakoof is a lifestyle fashion brand that makes trendy products for contemporary India, including T-shirts, phone covers, bags and hoodies. Revenue from the sale of these products remained the company’s main source of income during the year.
On the cost side, the cost of materials consumed remained the largest expense for the company. It increased 45.7% to Rs 134 crore in FY26 from Rs 92 crore in FY25. Employee benefit expenses rose 7.7% to Rs 28 crore, while marketing expenses increased 26.5% to Rs 62 crore. Transportation and handling expenses, however, fell 17.1% to Rs 29 crore from Rs 35 crore.
Depreciation expenses jumped nearly three times to Rs 16.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 6 crore in FY25. Other expenses also increased 66.1% to Rs 66.4 crore from Rs 40 crore.
Overall, Bewakoof’s total expenses increased 35.5% to Rs 336 crore in FY26 from Rs 248 crore in the previous fiscal year.
As a result, the company’s loss widened 19.4% to Rs 87.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 73.2 crore in FY25, despite the strong growth in revenue.
However, some operating metrics improved. Bewakoof’s EBITDA loss narrowed slightly to Rs 59.8 crore from Rs 60.7 crore in FY25, while its EBITDA margin improved to -24.6% from -35.1%. The company’s return on capital employed (ROCE) also improved to -63.4% in FY26 from -96.6% in FY25.


At the unit level, Bewakoof spent Rs 1.38 to earn every Rs 1 of operating revenue in FY26, compared with Rs 1.43 in the previous year.
Its total current assets stood at Rs 91.1 crore at the end of FY26, up from Rs 84.8 crore in FY25. Cash and bank balances increased slightly to Rs 22 lakh from Rs 18 lakh.
The strong revenue growth came in a year that also marked a leadership transition for Bewakoof.
Co-founder Prabhkiran Singh stepped down in February 2026 after 14 years with the company, a month before the end of FY26. Singh was therefore with the company for most of the fiscal year in which Bewakoof recorded 40% revenue growth.
The exit came three years after Aditya Birla Digital Fashion Ventures (ABDFVL) acquired a majority stake in Bewakoof in February 2023. ABDFVL is part of TMRW, the Aditya Birla Group’s digital-first fashion and lifestyle venture.

Kello cofounder Mona Gandhi was Airbnb’s first female engineer, while Reinforce Labs founder Anish Das Sarma previously led AI and machine learning teams as a Director at Google.
Peak XV said the latest Surge cohort reflects a shift towards AI becoming the underlying architecture of products, alongside startups rebuilding familiar consumer experiences and applying technology to physical infrastructure.
Surge provides seed stage startups with up to $5 million in funding along with support across hiring, product, engineering, go to market, marketing, communications, policy and global expansion.

summary:

summary:
Subway India operator EverBrands India has filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its initial public offering (IPO). The proposed IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 600 crore, with no offer for sale (OFS).
The company may also consider a pre-IPO placement of up to Rs 120 crore. If completed, the pre-IPO placement will reduce the size of the fresh issue. The company has proposed to list its equity shares on the BSE and NSE.
EverBrands operates Subway in India through Culinary Brands India Pvt Ltd (CBIPL). It also manages Lavazza Coffee and F&H Coffee and distributes Dilmah Tea in India through Fresh and Honest Cafe Pvt Ltd. The company operates Subway stores under both company-owned, company-operated (COCO) and franchisee-owned, franchisee-operated (FOFO) formats.
According to the DRHP, the company has appointed Motilal Oswal, ICICI Securities and Nuvama as book-running lead managers and MUFG as the registrar to the issue.
The company plans to use Rs 125 crore of the IPO proceeds to repay its borrowings. Another Rs 326.85 crore will be used for capital expenditure towards setting up new Subway stores under the COCO format, while the remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.
For FY26, revenue for EverBrands grew 34.9% year-on-year to Rs 966.17 crore from Rs 716.06 crore in FY25. Its quick service restaurant (QSR) business, which includes Subway, contributed Rs 693.09 crore during the fiscal year, while the company’s loss widened to Rs 58.19 crore from Rs 28.26 crore in FY25. EBITDA stood at Rs 98.13 crore, compared with Rs 64.21 crore in the previous fiscal.
As of FY26, EverBrands had 678 COCO and 330 FOFO Subway stores in India, along with eight FOFO stores in Sri Lanka. Its Subway business accounted for nearly 72% of the company’s total operating revenue during the fiscal.
EverBrands Ventures Pte Ltd is the largest shareholder of the company with a 57.78% stake on a fully diluted basis, followed by Norwest Capital LLC with 16.48%. Shivanand Shankar Mankekar HUF holds 5.83%, while Playbook India Fund II owns 4.15%. Enrich Agro Food Products and Bikramjit Singh Kandhari each hold 3.64% in the company on a fully diluted basis.
Earlier this year, EverBrands raised $15 million in a funding round led by Playbook Partners. The investment reportedly involved a 5% stake in Subway India’s parent at a valuation of around Rs 2,600-2,800 crore. The IPO price band and issue dates have not been announced yet.

title: Physical AI company SiMa.ai raises $150 Mn in Series C round
summary:
Physical AI company SiMa.ai has raised $150 million in a Series C financing round, bringing its total capital raised to $500 million and valuing the company at $1.45 billion. The round was co-led by Fidelity Management & Research Company and Amplify, with participation from Alter Venture Partners, Dell Technologies Capital and StepStone Group. AllianceBernstein, Baron Capital and J.P. Morgan also joined the round as new investors.
The proceeds will be used to scale Palette Neat, an agentic software environment for Physical AI, and develop next-generation hardware capable of delivering 1,000 TOPS of compute through purpose-built Physical AI silicon, SiMa.ai said in a press release.
Founded in 2018 by Krishna Rangasayee, SiMa.ai provides a software-centric platform for Physical AI applications. The company focuses on robotics, automotive, drones, industrial automation, aerospace and defence, smart vision and healthcare.
SiMa.ai said it serves more than 150 customers across automotive, drones and robotics, including ARK Electronics, AVerMedia, Bosch, Emerson, Intrinsic, Kontron, L&T Technology Services, Mistral, STIGA, Synopsys and Virya Autonomous Tech, among others.
According to market research cited by the company, the global Physical AI devices market, including robotics, automotive and drones, is projected to reach 145 million cumulative shipments by 2035.
SiMa.ai said Physical AI applications have traditionally relied on NVIDIA GPUs, which can be expensive and power intensive. The company offers a full-stack Physical AI platform that combines purpose-built silicon and software to simplify deployments.
Slated for H1 2028, the next-generation hardware will include machine learning IP, chiplets and SoCs. The company plans to target medium to high-end drones, humanoid robotics, automotive advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and AI-powered cockpits.

title: Ola Electric to raise up to Rs 1,000 Cr via rights issue
summary:
Electric two wheeler maker Ola Electric has approved a plan to raise up to Rs 1,000 crore through a rights issue of partly paid up equity shares.
The company’s board approved the proposal on September 28, subject to regulatory and statutory approvals. The issue will be open to eligible shareholders as of a record date, which will be announced later.
Ola Electric is yet to finalise the issue price, rights entitlement ratio, record date, issue timeline and payment terms. The number of shares to be issued will also be determined by the board.
The latest fundraise comes less than a month after Ola Electric approved a plan to raise up to Rs 1,500 crore through equity shares or convertible securities. The earlier fundraise could be carried out through a further public offer, rights issue, QIP, private placement or other permitted routes, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.
In June, Ola Electric raised Rs 780 crore through a QIP by allotting around 21.76 crore shares at Rs 35.86 apiece to qualified institutional buyers.
Meanwhile, Ola Electric COO Hyun Shik Park resigned from his position effective September 5, citing personal reasons.
The fresh fundraise comes as the EV two wheeler maker faces pressure on market share, customer complaints and its stock performance. In Q1 FY27, its revenue from operations fell 45% year on year to Rs 455 crore, while its net loss narrowed to Rs 336 crore from Rs 428 crore a year earlier. The company recorded 13,170 vehicle registrations in July, giving it a 6.8% market share.
Ola Electric has also been scaling up its battery cell manufacturing operations. The company recently secured Rs 95.81 crore under the government’s PLI Auto scheme for FY27. The board has also approved increasing Ola Electric’s authorised share capital from Rs 8,318.5 crore to Rs 8,721.9 crore, subject to shareholder approval.

title: Moneyview IPO sees nearly 100X subscription on final day
summary:
Digital lending platform Moneyview’s IPO saw strong investor demand, with the issue subscribed 98.5X on the final day of bidding. Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) led the demand, with their portion subscribed over 227X.
Moneyview’s initial public offering (IPO) was open for subscription from September 24-September 28, with a price band of Rs 32-34 and a minimum investment of Rs 14,112 for a lot size of 441 shares. 
The IPO comprises a fresh issue of Rs 750 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of up to 10.04 crore shares. At the upper price band, the issue is valued at around Rs 6,000 crore.
According to exchange data, the QIB portion was subscribed 227.5X, followed by non-institutional investors (NIIs) at 115.4X, while the retail portion saw 19.6X subscription.
Ahead of the IPO opening, Moneyview raised Rs 327.5 crore from anchor investors. The anchor book featured a mix of leading domestic mutual funds and global institutional investors including ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, Motilal Oswal Mutual Fund Goldman Sachs, Amundi Funds, 360 ONE, HDFC Life and others.
The company plans to deploy Rs 325 crore from the fresh issue towards loan disbursals, while Rs 250 crore will be infused into its NBFC subsidiary, Whizdm Finance. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.
Founded by Puneet Agarwal and Sanjay Aggarwal, Moneyview offers financial products including personal loans, insurance, credit cards, and digital gold through its network of banks, NBFCs, insurers, and other financial institutions.
Financially, Moneyview reported revenue of Rs 3,351 crore and a profit of Rs 244 crore in FY26. In the June 2026 quarter, its revenue grew 50.2% year-on-year to Rs 1,041 crore, while profit surged 158.8% to Rs 173.8 crore.

title: Entrackr’s The Spur D2C Mixer brings together over 40 founders and 10 investors
summary:
What happens when you bring together over 40 D2C founders, 10 investors, cocktails and dinner, and take away the usual panels and presentations?
You get conversations that are far more real.
Entrackr hosted The Spur, D2C Mixer, presented by Entrackr and PhonePe Gateway, in Gurugram on September 25, bringing together founders, investors and leaders from the D2C ecosystem for an informal evening of conversations, connections and, of course, a lot of fun.
There were no panels, no presentations and no fixed agenda. The idea was simple: step away from work for a few hours and connect with people who are building in the same ecosystem.
And that is exactly what happened.
Founders spoke openly about what they are building, the challenges they are facing, what is working, what is not and the realities of building a consumer brand. Investors also joined these conversations, making the evening a space for candid discussions rather than the usual pitch-and-network format.
From business challenges and industry trends to founder journeys, the conversations moved freely through the evening. There was plenty of networking, new introductions, laughter and some brutally honest discussions that may not always happen in a formal setting.
For Entrackr, however, the evening was about something bigger than just one mixer.
The D2C ecosystem is growing rapidly, and there is a growing need for founders to have a space where they can connect, share experiences, learn from each other and simply be around people who understand the journey.
The Spur is our attempt to build that space.
This was a great start, but this is only the beginning. We plan to bring the community together through more such intimate gatherings across the D2C ecosystem.
More founders. More conversations. More connections. And hopefully, a strong D2C family along the way.

title: SC declines stay on UPI MDR rollout, seeks response from Centre, RBI, NPCI on plea
summary:
The Supreme Court has declined to stay the October 15 rollout of the new Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) framework for specified UPI merchant transactions above Rs 2,000. The court has issued notices to the Centre, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) on a plea challenging the framework.
A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana directed the Centre, RBI and NPCI to file their responses within four weeks. The court also sought an explanation on the basis and legal character of the charge, according to Bar & Bench.
The plea, filed by advocate Anjan Datta, challenges the Centre's September 14 notification and the MDR framework announced on September 15. It questions the legal basis for imposing MDR on select UPI transactions and the manner in which the framework was introduced.
Under the new framework, a 0.4% MDR will apply to specified person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above Rs 2,000, capped at Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 and above. UPI payments to merchants of up to Rs 2,000 and person-to-person (P2P) transactions will continue to remain free.
Certain sectors, including railways, telecom, insurance, fuel and agricultural inputs, will attract a flat MDR of Rs 5 on transactions above Rs 2,000. Transactions involving mutual funds, securities, stockbrokers and dealers will carry an MDR of 0.02%, capped at Rs 300.
According to the Finance Ministry, the new framework will affect around 4% of merchant UPI transactions, leaving approximately 96% unaffected. The ministry has also clarified that MDR is neither a tax nor a charge collected by the government or NPCI, with the amount distributed among participants in the payments ecosystem.
The Finance Ministry has also said banks will ensure that merchants do not pass the MDR on to customers. The framework provides zero-MDR treatment to small merchants receiving up to Rs 1 lakh per month through UPI.
The new framework will end the zero-MDR regime for specified UPI merchant transactions that has been in place since 2020. The October 15 implementation remains in place following the Supreme Court's decision not to grant an interim stay.

The Jaipur-based company had earlier raised $2 million in a pre-Series A round led by Caspian Leap for Agriculture Fund, with participation from angels including Deepak Agarwal, Rishab Jain and Pulkit Bachhawat in May 2023.

Balwaan Krishi said around 86% of Indian farmers are small and marginal farmers cultivating less than two hectares. Its product portfolio is priced between Rs 10,000 and Rs 1 lakh, targeting this segment through a hybrid B2B and B2C distribution model.
The company plans to expand its manufacturing capabilities in India to improve control over product quality, supply chains and availability, while reducing dependence on imported machinery and components. It also plans to expand its presence in Southern India, with a focus on product availability and after-sales service.

title: D2C fashion brand The Indian Garage Co growth tapers down in FY26
summary:
As competition grows in India’s D2C fashion market, brands such as Snitch, Rare Rabbit, Bewakoof and The Souled Store are scaling rapidly. The Indian Garage Co (TIGC) saw its operating revenue grow 15% in FY26, much slower than the 2X growth it recorded in the previous year. However, its losses also increased 27% to Rs 29 crore during the year. 
TIGC’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 234.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 204.2 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

The Indian Garage Co is a D2C fashion firm that designs, manufactures, and sells men’s apparel under its in-house brands, catering to the mass-premium segment. Sale of products was its sole source of operating revenue. 
The company’s total income, including other income of Rs 2.95 crore, stood at Rs 237.5 crore during FY26 compared with Rs 206.9 crore in the previous fiscal year.
For the D2C brand, cost of materials remained the largest expenditure, rising 13% to Rs 117.5 crore in FY26 from Rs 104 crore in FY25. Advertising and promotional expenses more than doubled to Rs 29.3 crore in FY26 from Rs 14 crore in FY25 as the company stepped up spending amid rising competition in the fashion segment.
Job work charges, which include third-party vendors for outsourced manufacturing and production-related work, stood at Rs 39.5 crore, while employee benefits expenses rose 24% to Rs 21 crore during the fiscal year.
Depreciation and amortisation, finance costs, legal and professional fees, travel expenses, and other overheads pushed The Indian Garage Co’s total expenditure up 16% to Rs 276.1 crore in FY26 from Rs 237.5 crore in FY25.
With expenses continuing to outpace revenue, the Aditya Birla Digital-owned company’s losses widened during the fiscal year. Its losses increased 27% year-on-year to Rs 28.7 crore from Rs 22.6 crore in FY25.
On a unit level, the company spent Rs 1.18 to earn a rupee of operating revenue in FY26, compared with Rs 1.16 in the previous fiscal year. Its EBITDA margin improved marginally to -5.12% from -6% in FY25, while ROCE stood at -12.61%.

Aditya Birla Group’s TMRW invested around Rs 155 crore in TIGC in October 2023 and currently holds a 51% majority stake in the company. TMRW also holds a majority stake in fellow D2C apparel brand Bewakoof, which it acquired in December 2022.
The Indian Garage Co’s numbers point to a more difficult phase for scaled D2C fashion brands, where growth alone may not be enough to justify continued investment. As customer acquisition becomes more expensive and competition intensifies, brands need stronger retention, inventory discipline and operating leverage to build durable businesses. For TIGC, the larger question is whether its association with TMRW and the wider Aditya Birla ecosystem can help strengthen distribution and scale while improving the underlying economics of the business.

title: ED attaches Rs 442 Cr assets in RummyCulture case; total value stands at Rs 2,843 Cr
summary:
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has provisionally attached movable and immovable assets worth Rs 442 crore in its money laundering investigation involving Gameskraft Technologies and its online gaming platform RummyCulture, according to an ED press release.
The ED’s Bengaluru Zonal Office issued the provisional attachment order on September 25 under Section 5(1) of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002.
The assets attached include balances in fixed deposits, commercial shops, a villa and multiple residential properties. These assets are held in the names of family members, private family trusts and entities associated with shareholders of Gameskraft Technologies, according to the ED.
With the latest action, the total value of assets attached, frozen and seized in the case has reached around Rs 2,843 crore, the agency said.
The ED said its money laundering investigation was initiated based on multiple FIRs registered in Telangana for alleged cheating offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
Gameskraft Technologies and its associate entity RummyTime Technologies operated online real-money games, particularly rummy games and tournaments, through mobile applications including RummyCulture, RummyPrime, Playship and RummyTime.
According to the ED, these platforms had a user base of around 3 crore across India. The agency alleged that a significant number of users were from Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, where online real-money gaming had been banned.
The ED further alleged that the companies charged platform commissions of 10% to 15% on users’ staking or wagering amounts. It also alleged that automated programmes, or bots, were deployed against users without their knowledge or consent despite assurances that the platforms were free from such players.
According to the agency, the use of bots resulted in financial losses for users while generating proceeds of crime for the companies.
As per the ED, the proceeds generated through these activities were subsequently layered through dividend payments and share buybacks and invested in financial instruments and properties.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Sep 21 - Sep 26]
summary:
This week, 17 Indian startups raised $188.49 million across two growth-stage deals, 12 early-stage deals, and three undisclosed rounds. The week also saw 2 key appointments, one fund launch and one merger and acquisition.

In contrast, 17 startups had collectively secured about $61.8 million in the previous week.
[Growth-stage deals]
Growth-stage startups raised $162 million across just two deals this week. Electric mobility startup Ultraviolette secured $85 million in a round led by Yali Capital and TDK Ventures, with participation from Walden International chairman Lip-Bu Tan and existing investors. Enterprise AI startup Ema raised the remaining $77 million in a Series B round led by Creaegis. Ema was founded by Surojit Chatterjee, a former executive at Google and Coinbase.
[Early-stage deals]
Early-stage startups raised $26.49 million across 12 deals this week. Electric commercial mobility startup Drivn’s Indian entity raised Rs 45 crore ($4.7 million) in a seed round led by Avaana Capital. AI-powered health coaching platform Disha, formerly Curelink, secured Rs 43.88 crore in a Series A round led by General Catalyst, with participation from existing investor Elevation Capital.
Medicine quick-commerce platform Rio Health raised Rs 43.08 crore ($4.5 million) in a pre-Series A round led by Version One Ventures, with participation from Xeed Ventures, Good Capital and Amplify Partner. Proactive AI startup Sol raises $4 Mn from General Catalyst, Nexus VP, and others
Other funded startups included fintech and brokerage startup Definedge, lab-grown diamond jewellery startup ONYA, healthtech Betterhood, high-protein frozen food brand Protein Pantry and four others.
On-demand convenience platform TimBuckDo, Primary healthcare infrastructure company MyRx and Carry-first streetwear brand Indian Walker also raised funding this week, but did not disclose the amounts.
[City and segment-wise deals]
Bengaluru again led the funding charts with eight startup deals during the week, followed by Delhi-NCR with six deals. Pune, Goa and Hyderabad also recorded deals.

AI startups led the sectors with four deals, followed by healthtech and e-commerce startups which grabbed three deals each. Meanwhile Mobility, quick commerce, fintech, foodtech, lifestyle and HR Tech also saw funding activity.
[Series-wise deals]
Seed rounds led the week with six deals, followed by  pre-series A and pre-seed with four deals and three deals respectively. Series E, Series B, Series A and angel funding recorded one deal each.

[Week-on-week funding trend]
On a weekly basis, startup funding jumped over 3X to $188.49 million from $61.8 million raised in the previous week.
The average weekly funding over the past eight weeks stood at around $232.88 million across 21 deals.
[Key Hirings]
Only two key hirings were recorded this week. Digital lending platform Olyv appointed Ravi Sharma as its CFO. Sharma brings over 17 years of experience in financial services and previously served as CFO at Finova Capital.
Functional medicine company iThrive appointed Saloni Kulkarni, its former head of Client Services, to its Board of Directors.
[Mergers and Acquisitions]
Private equity firm Samara Capital has acquired stakes in Associated Road Carriers (ARC) and Calyx Container Terminals to build an integrated logistics platform.
[Fund Launches]
Early-stage VC firm Lavni Ventures has closed its second deep-tech impact fund at its Rs 200 crore ($21 million) target corpus, with an additional Rs 100 crore green-shoe option. The fund will back Indian deep-tech startups building scalable solutions across health and climate sectors.
[Financial results this week]

 
[New launches and partnerships]
▪️ SRM University AP launches UNITES Global Innovation Society
SRM University AP, in association with APSCHE, has launched the UNITES Global Innovation Society to bring together scientists, academia, industry, government and young researchers to address societal challenges. Hosted by the university’s Centre for Interdisciplinary Research, the initiative aims to promote collaborative research, innovation and scientific exchange across disciplines.
▪️ Nykaa and L’Oréal’s venture fund BOLD join hands to invest in Indian beauty startups
Nykaa has partnered with L’Oréal’s corporate venture capital fund, BOLD, to jointly invest in emerging Indian beauty and personal care brands. The two companies will acquire minority stakes in high-growth startups and provide strategic mentorship, combining L’Oréal’s global expertise with Nykaa’s retail and distribution network. Founders will retain operational and creative control of their businesses.
[News flash this week]
▪️ Pine Labs to Deploy 10 Lakh Soundboxes Across India to Power Digital Commerce
Pine Labs has announced a strategic investment to deploy 10 lakh Soundboxes across India to strengthen digital payments infrastructure. The initiative aims to expand UPI adoption across new markets and business segments as digital payments gain traction beyond small-ticket transactions.
▪️ MOS Utility subsidiary SIGN receives RBI's in-principle approval for online payment aggregator licence
MOS Utility subsidiary Samvriddhi Inclusive Growth Network (SIGN) has received RBI's in-principle approval to operate as an online payment aggregator. Subject to final authorisation, SIGN plans to offer UPI, card, QR-based and net banking payment solutions to merchants, with a focus on small businesses in rural and underserved markets.
▪️ NSE makes muted debut, lists at Rs 1,800 with 0.84% premium
The National Stock Exchange (NSE) made its stock market debut on Thursday, September 24, with its shares listing at Rs 1,800 on the BSE, a 0.84% premium over its IPO price of Rs 1,785. The listing follows NSE's Rs 22,561 crore IPO, which was subscribed 5.71 times, with bids for 50.58 crore shares against 8.86 crore shares on offer. The issue was entirely an offer for sale (OFS), with no proceeds going to NSE.
▪️ PB Fintech shares fall over 30% after IRDAI proposes lower insurance commissions
Shares of PB Fintech, the parent company of Policybazaar, plunged over 30% on Thursday after insurance regulator IRDAI proposed tighter commission caps and changes to insurance distribution rules. The stock fell to Rs 1,282 from its previous close of Rs 1,886.30, amid concerns that lower commissions could impact the earnings of insurance distributors. The proposed reforms cover life, health, and general insurance, along with stricter expense limits and greater transparency in insurance sales. 
▪️ Mastercard sells entire 4.31% Pine Labs stake for Rs 934 Cr
Mastercard exited Pine Labs by selling its entire 4.31% stake for Rs 933.5 crore through a bulk deal on Tuesday. ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, Societe Generale and Citigroup Global Markets Singapore were among the key buyers.
▪️ Spinny confidentially pre-files IPO; appoints Ex Bharti executive Akhil Gupta as board chairman
Used-car retailing platform Spinny has confidentially filed its draft IPO papers with SEBI, according to sources. The company plans to raise around Rs 2,500-3,000 crore through a mix of fresh issue and offer for sale (OFS), targeting a 2027 listing. Kotak Mahindra Capital, Morgan Stanley and Citigroup are working on the proposed IPO.
▪️ AceVector files RHP for Rs 287 Cr fresh issue, turns free cash flow positive in FY26
SoftBank-backed AceVector, the parent of Snapdeal and Unicommerce, has filed its RHP with SEBI for an IPO comprising a Rs 287 crore fresh issue and an OFS of up to 4.12 crore shares. Starfish I and Nexus entities will account for the majority of the OFS, while co-founders Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal will not sell their shares. The IPO follows AceVector turning free cash flow positive in FY26.

title: Accel, 360 ONE offload 4.07% stake in BlueStone for Rs 513 Cr via bulk deals
summary:
Venture capital firm Accel and investment firm 360 ONE have sold a combined 4.07% stake in jewellery retailer BlueStone for around Rs 513 crore through bulk and block deals.
According to BSE data, Accel India III (Mauritius) sold 28 lakh shares, representing a 1.84% stake, while funds managed by 360 ONE offloaded around 33.98 lakh shares, or a 2.23% stake. The shares were sold at Rs 827.60 per share, taking the total deal value to around Rs 513 crore.
As per the stock exchange, the shares were picked up by a mix of domestic and overseas institutional investors. Mirae Asset Mutual Fund bought around 20.8 lakh shares, while Nippon India Mutual Fund, SBI Life Insurance and Bajaj Life Insurance acquired around 9.5 lakh shares each.
Other buyers included Bandhan Mutual Fund, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup Global Markets Singapore and Kuwait Investment Authority.
Following the transaction, Accel’s holding through its affiliates declined to 8.71% from 10.55%. SBI Life’s stake, meanwhile, increased to 5.02% from 4.4% after it bought more than 9.5 lakh shares worth around Rs 79 crore.
This is the second major stake sale by Accel and 360 ONE in BlueStone this year. In June, Accel, 360 ONE and IvyCap Ventures sold shares worth around Rs 243 crore through multiple open-market transactions.
The stake sale comes at a time when BlueStone has been showing an improvement in its profitability. The jewellery retailer recently reported its third consecutive profitable quarter, following a sharp improvement in its financial performance.
In Q1 FY27, BlueStone reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 5.96 crore, compared with a net loss of Rs 34.74 crore in the same quarter last year. Its total income rose 49% year-on-year to Rs 751.81 crore during the quarter.
The company had also hit the 20% upper circuit following the announcement of its quarterly results.
Founded in 2011 by Gaurav Singh Kushwaha and Vidya Nataraj, BlueStone operates an omnichannel jewellery business and offers more than 8,000 designs across rings, pendants, earrings and other categories. The company had 352 stores across 139 cities as of June 2026.
BlueStone’s shares closed at Rs 809.30 on September 24, giving the company a total market capitalization of around Rs 12,364 crore ($1.3 billion).

title: Exclusive: Edtech startup Arivihan raising Rs 96 Cr at Rs 570 Cr valuation
summary:
AI Edtech startup Arivihan is set to raise Rs 95.86 crore or $10 million in a Series A round co-led by existing investors Accel and Prosus. This will be the second fundraise for the two-year-old firm in the past 15 months.

According to its regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr, the company’s board has approved the issuance of 4,648 Series A CCPS at an issue price of Rs 2,06,248.06 per share to raise the aforementioned amount.

Accel and Prosus will lead the round with an investment of Rs 47.48 crore each. Angel investors Dinesh Chandra Agrawal, Dinesh Gulati, Rajesh Sawhney (Founder and CEO of GSF Accelerator), and Gaurav Kapur collectively will invest around Rs 91 lakh in the round.
As per Entrackr’s estimates, Arivihan’s valuation has surged nearly 3.3X to around Rs 570 crore in its Series A round, compared to Rs 171 crore in the previous pre-Series A round.
According to the filings, the company plans to use the fresh capital to meet working capital requirements and support its expansion and growth.

The Indore-based company previously raised $4.17 million (around Rs 36 crore) in a pre-Series A round led by Prosus and Accel, with participation from GSF Investors.
Founded in 2024 by Ritesh Singh Chandel, Sonu Kumar and Rushabh Kothari, Arivihan offers AI-powered personalised learning for students in tier-II cities and rural areas, with coaching, doubt-solving and study plans for Class 12, CBSE and NEET.

title: Oziva spends Rs 246 Cr on marketing for Rs 463 Cr revenue in FY26
summary:
Hindustan Unilever-owned nutrition and wellness brand Oziva recorded strong revenue growth in FY26, months before the FMCG major acquired the remaining 49% stake in the company for Rs 824 crore. However, the growth came at the cost of profitability, as Oziva’s losses widened 4.4X during the year, steered largely by a sharp rise in advertising expenditure.
Oziva’s revenue from operations surged 80% to Rs 463.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 257.8 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

The company generates revenue from the sale of nutrition and wellness products across categories such as plant-based supplements, protein, vitamins, and products focused on skin and hair health.  These products were the sole source of operating revenue for the company.
Domestic sales remained Oziva’s primary revenue source, contributing Rs 454 crore in FY26, a 77% increase from Rs 257 crore in the previous fiscal year. International sales also increased to Rs 8.3 crore during the year, from just Rs 8.3 lakh in FY25.
Oziva also earned Rs 4.1 crore from non-operating activities, which pushed its total income to Rs 467.5 crore in FY26.
When it comes to spending, advertising and promotional expenditure more than doubled to Rs 246.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 119.8 crore in FY25. This alone accounted for over 51% of the company’s total expenses.
Cost of materials rose 63% to Rs 116 crore in FY26 from Rs 71 crore in FY25, while employee benefit expenses nearly doubled to Rs 45.4 crore. Transportation costs increased 57% to Rs 36.9 crore.
Other overheads, including legal and professional fees, IT expenses, travel, and miscellaneous costs, pushed Oziva’s total expenditure up 81% to Rs 482 crore in FY26 from Rs 266.9 crore in the previous fiscal year.
The steep rise in advertising and other costs weighed on the company’s bottom line. The company’s overall losses widened 4.4X to Rs 18.5 crore in FY26 from Rs 4.2 crore in FY25. Its EBITDA loss also increased to Rs 16.7 crore from Rs 6.3 crore, while EBITDA margin stood at -3.6%.

On a unit level, Oziva spent Rs 1.04 to earn a rupee of operating revenue in FY26. At the end of the fiscal year, its cash and bank balances declined 67% to Rs 8.8 crore, while current assets stood at Rs 106 crore.
In February this year, Hindustan Unilever acquired the remaining 49% stake in Oziva for Rs 824 crore, making it a wholly owned subsidiary. HUL had initially acquired a 51% stake in December 2022 for Rs 264.28 crore. The latest transaction valued Oziva at around Rs 1,682 crore, more than three times the valuation implied by HUL’s first investment.
Oziva operates in a crowded nutrition and wellness market, with competition from HealthKart, Wellbeing Nutrition, MuscleBlaze and The Whole Truth, along with larger FMCG companies expanding their health portfolios. Sustaining growth will require more disciplined customer acquisition and stronger repeat purchases rather than continued reliance on advertising. For HUL, its distribution and scale could help Oziva increase its reach, but improving customer economics and building brand loyalty will remain important as competition intensifies.

title: Amazon Now and Amazon Fresh report Rs 3,065 Cr revenue and Rs 1,158 Cr loss in FY26
summary:
Amazon’s quick commerce and grocery retail arm, Amazon Retail, which operates Amazon Now and Amazon Fresh, saw strong growth in revenue during FY26. However, the company’s losses widened sharply as expenses grew much faster than its business.
Amazon Retail’s revenue from operations jumped nearly 50% year-on-year to Rs 3,065 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 2,051 crore in FY25, according to its standalone financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

The company’s revenue primarily comes from the sale of goods through Amazon Now and Amazon Fresh, which remain its sole source of operating revenue. It also earned Rs 15 crore as other income, taking its total revenue to Rs 3,080 crore in FY26.
While the company managed to grow its top line, its cost structure remained heavy. The procurement of materials accounted for around 68% of Amazon Retail’s total expenses, which jumped nearly 65% to Rs 2,887 crore in FY26. This left the company with a gross margin of only around 5.08%.
Apart from procurement, the company spent Rs 529 crore on delivery charges during the fiscal year, while platform fees stood at Rs 248 crore. Legal expenses also remained significant at Rs 442 crore during FY26.
Overall, Amazon Retail’s total expenses surged 71.8% to Rs 4,239 crore in FY26 from Rs 2,468 crore in the previous fiscal year. This growth in expenses was considerably faster than its revenue growth.
As a result, the company’s net loss widened more than 3X to Rs 1,158 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 394 crore in FY25. On a unit economics basis, the company spent around Rs 1.38 to earn every rupee of revenue during the fiscal year.
The company’s operating performance also remained under pressure. Its EBITDA stood at negative Rs 1,136 crore, while its EBITDA margin and ROCE deteriorated to -37.06% and -235.22% in FY26.

The heavy losses come at a time when Amazon is stepping up investments in India’s quick commerce market, which has seen intense competition from Blinkit, Swiggy Instamart and Zepto.
According to a Reuters report, Amazon plans to invest $3 billion in India’s quick commerce business by 2030, marking its biggest bet yet on the segment. Of this, around $1 billion is expected to be invested by the end of 2027, followed by another $2 billion through 2030.
According to the company, Amazon’s quick commerce business has already crossed $1 billion in annualised gross sales over the past three months. Amazon described it as the fastest-growing e-commerce business in its India operations.
According to the report, Blinkit, Swiggy and Zepto together account for 77% of the quick commerce market, while Amazon has a 6.2% share. Amazon currently has around 750 quick commerce stores and is targeting roughly 1,300 stores by April next year.
Amazon’s quick commerce push highlights the capital intensity of competing in a market shaped by Blinkit, Swiggy Instamart and Zepto. For Amazon, the challenge is not merely building a larger fulfilment network, but reaching sufficient order density and improving margins across that network. The gap between revenue growth and expense growth suggests scale has yet to translate into operating leverage. Its ability to convert Amazon’s existing customer base into frequent quick commerce users will be critical to making the model economically viable.

title: Amazon Pay India’s FY26 losses widens to Rs 1,149 Cr despite double digit revenue growth
summary:
Amazon Pay India, the digital payments arm of e-commerce giant Amazon, continued to face profitability challenges in FY26, with its losses widening 33% despite a return to double-digit revenue growth after a decline in FY25. The company also witnessed intensifying competition in the UPI ecosystem, as newer players gained ground and its market share declined.
Amazon Pay India’s revenue from operations rose 18.5% year-on-year to Rs 2,484.4 crore in the fiscal year ended March 2026 from Rs 2,096.6 crore in FY25, according to its standalone financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Amazon Pay India enables users to make payments for shopping on Amazon and other services, including utility bills, mobile recharges, ticket bookings, and peer-to-peer UPI transfers. The company also offers digital wallets, insurance, and credit products.
Revenue from payment processing fees and commissions constitute its primary sources of income. 
Amazon Pay also earned Rs 108.2 crore from non-operating activities like interest on current investments which took its total income to Rs 2,592.6 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 2,195.1 crore in the previous fiscal year.
On the expense front, advertising and promotional costs remained the largest expenditure, rising 11% to Rs 1,767.6 crore in FY26. These costs included cashbacks, customer incentives, payments to banks for RuPay cards, advertising and publicity campaigns, B2B activities, and sponsorships. 
Payment processor fees surged 35% to Rs 1,140.6 crore, while employee benefit expenses increased 5% to Rs 224.9 crore, including Rs 55 crore in ESOP costs.
Communication expenses grew 30% to Rs 193.2 crore, while legal and professional charges stood at Rs 171.2 crore. The company incurred an additional Rs 243.6 crore in other overheads, including sales commissions and miscellaneous expenses, during the fiscal year.
Overall, Amazon Pay's total expenditure increased 22% to Rs 3,741.1 crore in FY26 from Rs 3,060.8 crore in FY25.
The rise in expenses, particularly payment processing fees and marketing costs, outpaced revenue growth, resulting in a 33% increase in net losses to Rs 1,148.5 crore in FY26 from Rs 865.7 crore in FY25. Its EBITDA loss also widened to Rs 1,227.4 crore from Rs 952.1 crore, with a negative EBITDA margin of 49.4%. The company's return on capital employed (ROCE) stood at -53.7%.

On a unit basis, Amazon Pay spent Rs 1.53 to earn every rupee of operating revenue during the fiscal year.
Despite its presence within Amazon's e-commerce ecosystem, Amazon Pay has struggled to maintain its position in India's rapidly expanding UPI market amid growing competition from newer players such as Navi and Flipkart-backed super.money, CRED.
According to NPCI data, Amazon Pay processed 95.93 million UPI transactions in August 2026, accounting for just 0.39% of the total transaction volume. PhonePe and Google Pay continued to dominate the market with a combined share of nearly 78%, while newer players have steadily expanded their presence.
Amazon Pay’s FY26 numbers show the limits of scale without stronger payment economics. The company remains heavily dependent on incentives and marketing to sustain its payments business, while rising processing costs add further pressure. This creates a difficult equation: higher transaction activity does not necessarily improve profitability when the cost of acquiring and processing payments remains costly. Its position within Amazon’s broader ecosystem provides reach, but translating that reach into a sustainable payments business remains the larger challenge.

title: MyRx raises seed round led by SteerX VC to expand primary healthcare infrastructure
summary:
Primary healthcare infrastructure company MyRx has raised an undisclosed amount in a seed funding round led by SteerX VC. 
The proceeds will be deployed for clinical network and technology infrastructure needed to make doctor-led primary care accessible at scale, MyRx said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2019 by Sourav Das, Surjit Das, and Neel Rath, MyRx is a primary healthcare infrastructure company that combines a doctor network with teleconsultation, electronic prescriptions and clinical workflow technology. It aims to make doctor-led primary care accessible through connected digital services and an expanding healthcare partner ecosystem.
According to MyRx, it is building shared healthcare infrastructure that connects patients, doctors and enterprise partners. By combining a clinical network with technology for consultation allocation, workflow monitoring and audit, MyRx aims to help partners expand healthcare access while maintaining visibility and accountability across service delivery.
The Hyderabad startup says that it  currently manages 35,000 teleconsultations a day and reports 15% month-on-month growth. title: PB Fintech shares fall over 30% after IRDAI proposes lower insurance commissions
summary:
The shares of PB Fintech, the parent company of Policybazaar, fell over 30% in Thursday’s trade after the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) proposed changes to insurance distribution and commission structures.
On the stock exchange, PB Fintech's stock fell from its previous close of Rs 1,886.30 to Rs 1,282 during the day.
The sell-off came after IRDAI released its consultation paper on September 23. The regulator has proposed product- and channel-wise caps on commissions across life, health and general insurance.
For individual life insurance policies with a premium-payment term of 10 years or more, IRDAI has proposed a first-year commission cap of 20% for distribution entities and 25% for individual agents. For policies with a six-to-eight-year premium-payment term, the proposed caps are lower at 14% for distribution entities and 17.5% for agents.
For individual pure-term insurance policies with multi-year premiums, the proposed first-year commission is 25% for distribution entities and 30% for agents. Renewal commissions would be capped at 7.5% and 10%, respectively.
The proposal also covers health insurance. For individual health policies, the first-year commission has been proposed at 15% for distribution entities and 20% for agents. Renewal and portability commissions would be capped at 5% for distribution entities and 10% for agents.
Motor insurance will also see tighter limits. IRDAI has proposed zero commission for distribution entities on third-party motor insurance. For new vehicles, commission on own-damage, personal accident and legal liability covers has been proposed at 5% for distribution entities and 10% for agents and associates.
The proposed changes could impact PB Fintech as Policybazaar earns revenue by distributing insurance products. Lower commission caps could reduce the amount distributors earn on new policies and renewals, putting pressure on their take-rates and earnings.
IRDAI said the proposed framework would link commissions to factors such as product complexity and the effort required to sell the policy. It also proposes counting different forms of distributor payments to prevent companies from bypassing the commission limits.
However, the proposed commission structure is not final yet. IRDAI has invited feedback from stakeholders before taking the proposals forward.

title: Moneyview raises Rs 327 Cr from anchor investors ahead of IPO
summary:
Digital lending platform Moneyview has raised Rs 327.5 crore from anchor investors ahead of its Rs 1,092 crore initial public offering (IPO), which opens for public subscription today (September 24).
The Bengaluru-based fintech allotted 9.63 crore shares at Rs 34 apiece, the upper end of its IPO price band, to anchor investors on September 23. The company raised the amount from 12 anchor investors, including several large mutual funds and institutional investors.
Domestic mutual funds accounted for the bulk of the anchor allocation. SBI Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, Motilal Oswal Mutual Fund, Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund and Quant Mutual Fund were among the investors participating in the anchor book. Goldman Sachs, Amundi Funds, 360 ONE, HDFC Life and India Acorn Fund also invested in the IPO.
Moneyview's IPO comes with a price band of Rs 32-34 per share and will remain open until September 28. The issue comprises a fresh issue of Rs 750 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of around 10.04 crore shares worth Rs 341.6 crore at the upper end of the price band.
The company plans to use Rs 325 crore from the fresh issue to support loan disbursals under default loss guarantee (DLG) arrangements. Another Rs 250 crore will be invested in its NBFC subsidiary Whizdm Finance to strengthen its capital base. The remaining funds will be used for general corporate purposes.
At the upper end of the price band, Moneyview is looking at a post-issue valuation of around Rs 6,000 crore. This is significantly lower than the valuation of about $1.2 billion it commanded after its last equity funding round in 2024, according to Inc42.
The fintech reported Rs 3,351 crore in revenue and Rs 244 crore in profit in FY26. In the June 2026 quarter, its revenue rose 50.2% year-on-year to Rs 1,041 crore, while profit jumped 158.8% to Rs 173.8 crore.
Moneyview, founded by Puneet Agarwal and Sanjay Aggarwal, offers financial products such as personal loans, insurance, credit cards, and digital gold through its network of banks, NBFCs, insurers, and other financial institutions.

title: NSE makes muted debut, lists at Rs 1,800 with 0.84% premium
summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) made its stock market debut on Thursday, September 24, with its shares listing at Rs 1,800 on the BSE. This is a 0.84% premium over its IPO price of Rs 1,785.
The listing comes after NSE’s Rs 22,561 crore IPO, which was subscribed 5.71 times during the three-day bidding process. The issue received bids for 50.58 crore shares against 8.86 crore shares on offer.
The IPO was priced in the range of Rs 1,700-1,785 per share, with the company fixing the final price at the upper end of the band. The minimum lot size was eight shares, taking the minimum investment to Rs 14,280.
The issue was entirely an offer for sale (OFS), meaning existing shareholders sold their shares while NSE itself did not receive any funds from the IPO.
The qualified institutional buyers (QIB) portion was subscribed 12.68 times, while the non-institutional investor (NII) category saw 6.55 times subscription. In comparison, the retail portion was subscribed 1.39 times.
The much-hyped NSE IPO, however, did not deliver a big listing pop. The shares listed at Rs 1,800, just 0.84% above the issue price of Rs 1,785. This was lower than the premium indicated by grey market trends ahead of the debut, which had pointed to a listing price of around Rs 1,825-1,865. 
NSE is India's largest stock exchange and has a dominant share of the country's equity and derivatives trading. It had more than 129 million registered investors as of March 2026.
The share price is currently tarded at Rs 1,862 (as of 10.26 AM), with the total market capitalization of Rs 4,60,845 crore.

The startup will use the funds for product and infrastructure development, hiring across engineering and research, GPU compute and training data. It also plans to build enterprise grade security, privacy and on premises infrastructure for customers.

The platform is designed for engineers working on mission critical applications across defence, aerospace, robotics, high frequency trading, finance, embedded systems, automotive and semiconductors.
ByteAsk aims to address the limitations of existing AI coding tools in C and C++ development, particularly in environments where reliability, performance and correctness are critical.
The startup cited industry estimates that put C++ at around $400 billion in annual engineering salary spend. It sees agentic coding as a roughly $10 billion opportunity that is growing rapidly.
ByteAsk plans to initially target large enterprises in high frequency trading, automotive and embedded systems before expanding into adjacent markets. On its internal benchmark based on real firmware engineering tickets, ByteAsk said its grounding environment enabled a smaller model to resolve 89% of tickets, compared with 61% for the best frontier model tested without the environment.
The startup is also developing a post training approach for C++, with plans to release a language model specifically post trained for C++ within the next six to eight months.

title: On-demand convenience platform TimBuckDo raises bridge round at Rs 150 Cr valuation
summary:
On-demand convenience platform TimBuckDo has raised an undisclosed amount in a bridge funding round at a post-money valuation of Rs 150 crore. The round was backed by Srinath Setty through his family office Trasa Ventures and Adarsh Narahari.
The Bengaluru-based startup is preparing to raise its Series A round in the coming months, TimBuckDo said in a press release.
Prior to this, TimBuckDo had raised around Rs 6.6 crore in a seed round last year from Nandkishore Kalambi, Morton Meyerson, Arjun Vaidya, Anupam Bansal, Sandesh Sharda, Rukam Capital, IDEABAAZ, its founders and TurboStart.
The fresh capital will be used to support the company’s next phase of expansion as it works towards its Series A round.
Founded in 2022 by Mythri Kumar and Apoorv Sharma Prasad, TimBuckDo is building an on-demand convenience marketplace powered by verified college students, or “Doers”. The platform connects households and businesses with students for services including elder companionship, pet care, child support, home business assistance and other everyday needs.
The company is also focused on creating flexible earning opportunities for college students alongside their education. It is targeting around Rs 400 crore in gross revenue and more than 10,000 household orders per day across India over the next three years.
The broader on-demand convenience space has also seen investor interest. Pronto raised $25 million in a Series B round in March to expand its household-help platform, while AI concierge startup Hulp raised $2.6 million in a seed round in August to offer human-assisted support for household and lifestyle tasks.

title: RPS Ventures sells 0.83% stake in Meesho for Rs 900 Cr through block deals
summary:
RPS Ventures, an early investor in e-commerce platform Meesho, offloaded 3.86 crore shares in the Bengaluru-based company for around Rs 900 crore through multiple block deals on the BSE on Wednesday.
According to stock exchange data, RPS Ventures through RPS WOS II LLC offloaded 3,86,13,960 equity shares at Rs 233 per share, representing approximately 0.83% stake in Meesho. The transaction was valued at Rs 899.71 crore.
RPS Ventures, a fund founded by former SoftBank Vision Fund managing partner Kabir Misra, held a 1.12% stake in Meesho as of June 2026. Following the latest transaction, its holding is estimated to have declined to around 0.29%.
The shares were acquired by a mix of domestic and foreign institutional investors. The Government of Singapore emerged as the largest buyer, acquiring 1.32 crore shares worth approximately Rs 307.5 crore, followed by Mirae Asset Mutual Fund, which purchased 77.21 lakh shares worth Rs 179.9 crore.
Other buyers included Societe Generale, BNP Paribas, Fidelity Advisor Overseas Fund, Citigroup Global Markets Singapore, Norges Bank on account of the Government Pension Fund Global, Ghisallo Master Fund, Morgan Stanley Asia Singapore, WhiteOak Capital Mutual Fund, Bajaj Life Insurance and Edelweiss Mutual Fund.
The transaction follows a series of stake sales by Meesho's early investors. Earlier this month, Japanese investment giant SoftBank sold 8 crore shares, representing a 1.73% stake worth Rs 1,650.4 crore. SoftBank held an 8.60% stake in the company as of June 2026.
In August, Peak XV Partners and Elevation Capital offloaded a combined 2.27% stake in Meesho through block deals worth around Rs 1,949 crore. This was followed by Y Combinator's stake sale worth approximately Rs 970 crore.
Meesho reported a 48% year-on-year growth in operating revenue to Rs 3,713 crore in Q1 FY27, while its net loss narrowed 54% to Rs 133 crore from Rs 289 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
At the end of Wednesday's trading session, Meesho's shares closed at Rs 236.35 on the BSE, with a total market capitalization of Rs 1,09,341 crore ($11.5 billion).
